title: Solution document (assistant.json), format 0.1
description: How a solution's parts fit together. A solution is an Agent Plugins v1.0.0 plugin whose plugin.json names this file in extensions["org.sigrix"].assistant; Bailey reads it to install and run the solution, and any builder may write it. This schema is the writer's contract: a document a writer emits validates against it. A reader is wider, as schemas/README.md says: it ignores a member it does not know and refuses a major version it does not know. Every path is relative to the plugin's root, uses forward slashes, and names a file the plugin carries.

format_version.description: The format this document is written in, as MAJOR.MINOR. A minor version only adds optional members, so a reader that knows the major reads the document by ignoring what it does not know. A change a reader cannot ignore moves the major, and a reader refuses a major it does not know.

name.description: The plugin's name, equal to plugin.json's name, in the Agent Plugins v1.0.0 name grammar.

title.description: The name a person sees, such as "Shop Support".

description.description: One or two sentences on the job the solution does. Absent and empty both mean there is none.

instructions.description: The skill holding the assistant's own instructions. A client keeps its body in context from the first message, where the skills in skills load when they are needed. It is not also listed in skills.

persona.description: A Markdown file holding the voice the assistant answers in, kept in context with the instructions. A writer may instead open the instructions with the voice, and then leaves this member out.

starters.description: Messages a client may offer to start a conversation with, in the order given.

skills.description: The Agent Skills the plugin carries besides the instructions. A client loads a skill's body when the conversation needs it.

skills_sold_separately.description: The names of skills the assistant uses that the plugin does not carry, which the person obtains on their own. A client may say so at install, and the assistant works without them.

mcp.description: The plugin's MCP configuration, mcp.json in the Agent Plugins layout. Absent when the assistant uses no MCP server.

tools.description: For each server in the MCP configuration, keyed by its name there, the tools the writer declared and which of them write. A client asks before a write, and treats as a write any tool missing from its server's declaration, and every tool of a server missing from this map.

examples.description: Inputs the assistant is meant to handle, each with the answer it should give when the writer has one. A client may run them to check an install.

knowledge.description: The documents the solution asks the person for, its knowledge slots, which a client asks for at install the way it asks for keys. The documents stay on the person's machine and never go into a package.

skill_name.description: An Agent Skills name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, neither starting nor ending with a hyphen, and without the words anthropic or claude, which clients reserve.

skill_path.description: A skill's SKILL.md in the Agent Plugins layout, skills/<name>/SKILL.md, where <name> is the name in its frontmatter and so follows skill_name.

file_path.description: A file inside the plugin: relative, with forward slashes, and with no segment that starts with a dot, so no path climbs out of the plugin or names a hidden file.

tool_name.description: A tool's name as its MCP server lists it.

tools.description: The server's tools the writer declared.

write_tools.description: The declared tools that change something outside the conversation. Each is also in tools.

output.description: An answer of the kind the assistant should give. Absent and empty both mean the writer gave none.

name.description: The slot's name, unique in this document, such as refund_policy.

description.description: What the person should supply, in words they would use.

accepts.description: The file extensions the slot takes, lowercase and without the dot, such as pdf or csv.

required.description: Whether the solution needs the document before it runs. Absent means false.
